items.name: The first recorded ancient Olympic Games
items.blurb: The first recorded ancient Olympic Games (776 BC). Tradition dates the first Games at Olympia, in Greece, to 776 BC.

items.name: The Battle of Marathon
items.blurb: The Battle of Marathon (490 BC). Athens defeated a Persian invasion force on the plain of Marathon.

items.name: The Battle of Thermopylae
items.blurb: The Battle of Thermopylae (480 BC). A small Greek force led by 300 Spartans held a narrow pass against the Persian army.

items.name: Qin Shi Huang unifies China
items.blurb: Qin Shi Huang unifies China (221 BC). The state of Qin conquered its rivals, creating the first unified Chinese empire.

items.name: The assassination of Julius Caesar
items.blurb: The assassination of Julius Caesar (44 BC). Roman senators stabbed Caesar to death on the Ides of March.

items.name: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
items.blurb: Vesuvius buries Pompeii (AD 79). The volcano's eruption buried the Roman towns of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.

items.name: Work begins on Hadrian's Wall
items.blurb: Work begins on Hadrian's Wall (AD 122). The Roman emperor Hadrian ordered a wall across northern Britain.

items.name: The fall of the Western Roman Empire
items.blurb: The fall of the Western Roman Empire (AD 476). The last western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed.

items.name: Vikings raid Lindisfarne
items.blurb: Vikings raid Lindisfarne (AD 793). A Viking raid on the island monastery is often taken as the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

items.name: Charlemagne is crowned emperor
items.blurb: Charlemagne is crowned emperor (AD 800). The pope crowned the Frankish king Emperor of the Romans on Christmas Day.

items.name: The Battle of Hastings
items.blurb: The Battle of Hastings (1066). William of Normandy defeated King Harold II and conquered England.

items.name: Magna Carta is sealed
items.blurb: Magna Carta is sealed (1215). King John agreed to a charter limiting royal power, at Runnymede.

items.name: The Black Death reaches Europe
items.blurb: The Black Death reaches Europe (1347). Bubonic plague arrived in Europe and killed perhaps a third of its people within a few years.

items.name: The fall of Constantinople
items.blurb: The fall of Constantinople (1453). Ottoman forces captured the Byzantine capital, ending the Eastern Roman Empire.

items.name: The Battle of Bosworth Field
items.blurb: The Battle of Bosworth Field (1485). Henry Tudor defeated Richard III, beginning the Tudor dynasty.

items.name: Columbus reaches the Americas
items.blurb: Columbus reaches the Americas (1492). Christopher Columbus landed in the Bahamas while trying to reach Asia by sailing west.

items.name: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses
items.blurb: Martin Luther's Ninety-five Theses (1517). Luther's challenge to the Church helped launch the Protestant Reformation.

items.name: The first voyage around the world is completed
items.blurb: The first voyage around the world is completed (1522). The survivors of Ferdinand Magellan's expedition returned to Spain; Magellan himself died on the way.

items.name: The defeat of the Spanish Armada
items.blurb: The defeat of the Spanish Armada (1588). A Spanish invasion fleet sent against England was beaten and scattered by storms.

items.name: The Gunpowder Plot
items.blurb: The Gunpowder Plot (1605). Plotters including Guy Fawkes tried and failed to blow up the English Parliament.

items.name: The Mayflower reaches America
items.blurb: The Mayflower reaches America (1620). English Pilgrims sailed to found Plymouth Colony in what is now Massachusetts.

items.name: The Peace of Westphalia
items.blurb: The Peace of Westphalia (1648). Treaties ended the Thirty Years' War in Europe.

items.name: King Charles I is executed
items.blurb: King Charles I is executed (1649). After the English Civil War, the king was beheaded in London.

items.name: The Great Fire of London
items.blurb: The Great Fire of London (1666). A fire starting in a bakery on Pudding Lane destroyed much of the city.

items.name: England and Scotland unite
items.blurb: England and Scotland unite (1707). The Acts of Union created the Kingdom of Great Britain.

items.name: Captain Cook reaches Botany Bay
items.blurb: Captain Cook reaches Botany Bay (1770). James Cook's ship Endeavour landed on the east coast of Australia.

items.name: The Boston Tea Party
items.blurb: The Boston Tea Party (1773). American colonists dumped British tea into Boston Harbor in protest at taxes.

items.name: The US Declaration of Independence
items.blurb: The US Declaration of Independence (1776). Thirteen American colonies declared themselves independent from Britain.

items.name: The First Fleet arrives in Australia
items.blurb: The First Fleet arrives in Australia (1788). British ships carrying convicts founded a colony at Sydney Cove.

items.name: The storming of the Bastille
items.blurb: The storming of the Bastille (1789). Parisians stormed a royal fortress and prison, a key moment of the French Revolution.

items.name: King Louis XVI is executed
items.blurb: King Louis XVI is executed (1793). The French king was guillotined during the Revolution.

items.name: The Louisiana Purchase
items.blurb: The Louisiana Purchase (1803). The United States bought a vast territory west of the Mississippi from France.

items.name: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
items.blurb: Napoleon crowns himself emperor (1804). Napoleon took the crown from the pope's hands at Notre-Dame in Paris.

items.name: The Battle of Trafalgar
items.blurb: The Battle of Trafalgar (1805). Nelson's British fleet defeated a French and Spanish fleet; Nelson was killed.

items.name: Britain abolishes the slave trade
items.blurb: Britain abolishes the slave trade (1807). Parliament banned the trade in enslaved people across the British Empire.

items.name: The Battle of Waterloo
items.blurb: The Battle of Waterloo (1815). Napoleon was finally defeated by Wellington and Blücher.

items.name: The first public steam railway opens
items.blurb: The first public steam railway opens (1825). The Stockton and Darlington Railway in England carried passengers behind a steam locomotive.

items.name: The Great Famine begins in Ireland
items.blurb: The Great Famine begins in Ireland (1845). Potato blight caused a famine that killed about a million people.

items.name: The California Gold Rush
items.blurb: The California Gold Rush (1848). The discovery of gold at Sutter's Mill drew hundreds of thousands of people west.

items.name: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
items.blurb: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species (1859). Charles Darwin set out his theory of evolution by natural selection.

items.name: The American Civil War begins
items.blurb: The American Civil War begins (1861). Fighting broke out between the Union and the Confederate states.

items.name: The Emancipation Proclamation
items.blurb: The Emancipation Proclamation (1863). Abraham Lincoln declared enslaved people in the Confederate states to be free.

items.name: Abraham Lincoln is assassinated
items.blurb: Abraham Lincoln is assassinated (1865). The president was shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington.

items.name: The Meiji Restoration in Japan
items.blurb: The Meiji Restoration in Japan (1868). Imperial rule was restored and Japan began rapid modernisation.

items.name: The Suez Canal opens
items.blurb: The Suez Canal opens (1869). The canal linked the Mediterranean and Red Seas, shortening the route from Europe to Asia.

items.name: Bell patents the telephone
items.blurb: Bell patents the telephone (1876). Alexander Graham Bell received a patent for the telephone.

items.name: Krakatoa erupts
items.blurb: Krakatoa erupts (1883). A huge volcanic eruption in Indonesia was heard thousands of kilometres away.

items.name: The Eiffel Tower is completed
items.blurb: The Eiffel Tower is completed (1889). The tower was built as the entrance to the World's Fair in Paris.

items.name: The first modern Olympic Games
items.blurb: The first modern Olympic Games (1896). The modern Olympics began in Athens.

items.name: The Wright brothers' first powered flight
items.blurb: The Wright brothers' first powered flight (1903). Orville and Wilbur Wright flew at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

items.name: The San Francisco earthquake
items.blurb: The San Francisco earthquake (1906). An earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of the city.

items.name: The Titanic sinks
items.blurb: The Titanic sinks (1912). The liner struck an iceberg on its first voyage and sank with the loss of about 1,500 lives.

items.name: The First World War begins
items.blurb: The First World War begins (1914). War broke out in Europe after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.

items.name: The Panama Canal opens
items.blurb: The Panama Canal opens (1914). The canal linked the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans across Panama.

items.name: The Lusitania is sunk
items.blurb: The Lusitania is sunk (1915). A German submarine sank the British liner off Ireland.

items.name: The Battle of the Somme
items.blurb: The Battle of the Somme (1916). One of the bloodiest battles in history was fought in northern France.

items.name: The Russian Revolution
items.blurb: The Russian Revolution (1917). The Bolsheviks led by Lenin seized power in Russia.

items.name: The First World War ends
items.blurb: The First World War ends (1918). An armistice ended the fighting at 11 am on 11 November.

items.name: The Treaty of Versailles
items.blurb: The Treaty of Versailles (1919). The peace treaty set the terms for Germany after the First World War.

items.name: Tutankhamun's tomb is discovered
items.blurb: Tutankhamun's tomb is discovered (1922). Howard Carter found the almost untouched tomb in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.

items.name: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin
items.blurb: Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin (1928). Fleming noticed mould killing bacteria in a dish in his London laboratory.

items.name: The Wall Street Crash
items.blurb: The Wall Street Crash (1929). A stock market collapse in New York helped trigger the Great Depression.

items.name: The first FIFA World Cup
items.blurb: The first FIFA World Cup (1930). Uruguay hosted and won the first football World Cup.

items.name: Hitler becomes chancellor of Germany
items.blurb: Hitler becomes chancellor of Germany (1933). The Nazi leader was appointed chancellor and soon became dictator.

items.name: The Hindenburg disaster
items.blurb: The Hindenburg disaster (1937). A German passenger airship caught fire while landing in New Jersey.

items.name: The Second World War begins
items.blurb: The Second World War begins (1939). Germany invaded Poland; Britain and France declared war.

items.name: The attack on Pearl Harbor
items.blurb: The attack on Pearl Harbor (1941). Japan attacked the US naval base in Hawaii, bringing the US into the war.

items.name: D-Day: the Normandy landings
items.blurb: D-Day: the Normandy landings (1944). Allied troops landed on the beaches of Normandy in France.

items.name: Atomic bombs are dropped on Japan
items.blurb: Atomic bombs are dropped on Japan (1945). The US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

items.name: The United Nations is founded
items.blurb: The United Nations is founded (1945). The UN was set up after the Second World War to keep international peace.

items.name: India and Pakistan become independent
items.blurb: India and Pakistan become independent (1947). British rule ended and the subcontinent was divided into two countries.

items.name: The NHS is founded
items.blurb: The NHS is founded (1948). Britain's National Health Service began offering free healthcare.

items.name: The People's Republic of China is proclaimed
items.blurb: The People's Republic of China is proclaimed (1949). Mao Zedong declared the new state in Beijing.

items.name: The Korean War begins
items.blurb: The Korean War begins (1950). North Korea invaded South Korea.

items.name: Everest is climbed for the first time
items.blurb: Everest is climbed for the first time (1953). Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth II is crowned
items.blurb: Queen Elizabeth II is crowned (1953). The coronation was watched on television by millions.

items.name: Rosa Parks and the Montgomery bus boycott
items.blurb: Rosa Parks and the Montgomery bus boycott (1955). Rosa Parks's arrest for keeping her bus seat sparked a year-long boycott.

items.name: Sputnik, the first satellite, is launched
items.blurb: Sputnik, the first satellite, is launched (1957). The Soviet Union put the first artificial satellite into orbit.

items.name: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first person in space
items.blurb: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first person in space (1961). The Soviet cosmonaut orbited the Earth once.

items.name: The Berlin Wall is built
items.blurb: The Berlin Wall is built (1961). East Germany sealed off West Berlin with a wall.

items.name: The Cuban Missile Crisis
items.blurb: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962). The US and the Soviet Union came close to nuclear war over missiles in Cuba.

items.name: Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech
items.blurb: Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech (1963). King spoke to about 250,000 people at the Lincoln Memorial.

items.name: President Kennedy is assassinated
items.blurb: President Kennedy is assassinated (1963). John F. Kennedy was shot in Dallas, Texas.

items.name: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
items.blurb: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon (1969). Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon.

items.name: The Apollo 13 rescue
items.blurb: The Apollo 13 rescue (1970). An explosion forced the crew to abandon their Moon landing and loop home safely.

items.name: Richard Nixon resigns
items.blurb: Richard Nixon resigns (1974). The US president resigned over the Watergate scandal.

items.name: Concorde begins passenger flights
items.blurb: Concorde begins passenger flights (1976). The supersonic airliner entered service with British Airways and Air France.

items.name: Mount St. Helens erupts
items.blurb: Mount St. Helens erupts (1980). The volcano in Washington State blew out its side in a huge eruption.

items.name: The Challenger disaster
items.blurb: The Challenger disaster (1986). The space shuttle broke apart shortly after launch.

items.name: The Chernobyl disaster
items.blurb: The Chernobyl disaster (1986). A reactor exploded at a nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine.

items.name: The fall of the Berlin Wall
items.blurb: The fall of the Berlin Wall (1989). Crowds crossed and began tearing down the wall as East Germany opened its borders.

items.name: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched
items.blurb: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched (1990). The telescope was carried into orbit by a space shuttle.

items.name: Germany is reunified
items.blurb: Germany is reunified (1990). East and West Germany became one country again.

items.name: The Soviet Union breaks up
items.blurb: The Soviet Union breaks up (1991). The USSR split into fifteen independent countries.

items.name: Nelson Mandela becomes president of South Africa
items.blurb: Nelson Mandela becomes president of South Africa (1994). South Africa's first fully democratic election ended apartheid rule.

items.name: The Channel Tunnel opens
items.blurb: The Channel Tunnel opens (1994). A rail tunnel linked Britain and France under the sea.

items.name: Dolly the sheep is born
items.blurb: Dolly the sheep is born (1996). Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

items.name: Hong Kong is handed back to China
items.blurb: Hong Kong is handed back to China (1997). Britain returned Hong Kong to China after more than 150 years.

items.name: Wikipedia is launched
items.blurb: Wikipedia is launched (2001). The free online encyclopedia anyone can edit went live.

items.name: The September 11 attacks
items.blurb: The September 11 attacks (2001). Hijacked planes destroyed the World Trade Center in New York.

items.name: Euro notes and coins come into use
items.blurb: Euro notes and coins come into use (2002). Twelve European countries switched to euro cash.

items.name: The Human Genome Project is completed
items.blurb: The Human Genome Project is completed (2003). Scientists finished mapping nearly all human genes.

items.name: Facebook is founded
items.blurb: Facebook is founded (2004). Mark Zuckerberg and fellow students launched it at Harvard.

items.name: The Indian Ocean tsunami
items.blurb: The Indian Ocean tsunami (2004). An undersea earthquake caused tsunamis that killed about 230,000 people.

items.name: The first iPhone goes on sale
items.blurb: The first iPhone goes on sale (2007). Apple released its first smartphone.

items.name: Barack Obama is elected US president
items.blurb: Barack Obama is elected US president (2008). Obama became the first African American president.

items.name: The Higgs boson is discovered
items.blurb: The Higgs boson is discovered (2012). Scientists at CERN announced the long-sought particle.

items.name: London hosts the Olympics for the third time
items.blurb: London hosts the Olympics for the third time (2012). London had also hosted the Games in 1908 and 1948.

items.name: The Brexit referendum
items.blurb: The Brexit referendum (2016). UK voters chose to leave the European Union.

items.name: COVID-19 is declared a pandemic
items.blurb: COVID-19 is declared a pandemic (2020). The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a pandemic in March.

items.name: The James Webb Space Telescope is launched
items.blurb: The James Webb Space Telescope is launched (2021). The powerful infrared telescope was launched on Christmas Day.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth II dies
items.blurb: Queen Elizabeth II dies (2022). She died at Balmoral after a reign of 70 years.
